claims.claim_text: Institutional and obituary evidence strongly identify the indexed Magda Pollaczek as the Bryn Mawr graduate later known as Magda Tisza who served with OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare maiden name, graduation chronology, and explicit OSS service agree across institutional and obituary sources.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence rare-name match with explicit OSS linkage in two reputable sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: The institutional biography dates graduation, the intervening teaching year, and OSS work to 1943-1944.
claims.match_notes: The later married name Magda Tisza is recorded as a documented variant.

claims.claim_text: Magda Pollaczek taught French and German at Dana Hall for a year immediately before beginning OSS work in 1944.
claims.evidence_excerpt: hired to teach French for a year at Dana Hall
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional chronology places the Dana Hall teaching year between her 1943 graduation and 1944 OSS work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity through the rare maiden name and explicit OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly sequenced as the intervening one-year job before OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Dana Hall is employment; Bryn Mawr is separately modeled as student status.

claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate in the institutional chronology.
